title: Knowing The Spec to Explore The Design via Transformed Bayesian Optimization
problem: Existing chip design space exploration methods aim for optimal Pareto-front designs but neglect design specifications, leading to infeasible or un-produceable architectures. This paper addresses finding optimal RISC-V SoC designs for LLM inference that meet specified performance targets.
motivation: As AI chips scale rapidly for LLMs, efficient design space exploration that respects manufacturing constraints and performance specifications is critical.
method: The framework employs a transformed Gaussian process (GP) model that prioritizes specified target metrics, combined with a customized EHRM acquisition function for multi-objective optimization. The approach explores RISC-V SoC architecture design spaces for LLM workloads including Transformer, BERT, and GPT-1.
key_novelty: A spec-driven transformed Bayesian optimization framework that incorporates design specifications as constraints in the Gaussian process model to guide architecture exploration.
contributions: Proposed Spec-driven transformed Bayesian optimization framework for architecture DSE
Tailored transformed Gaussian process model that prioritizes specified target metrics
Customized EHRM acquisition function for multi-objective architecture optimization
Demonstrates 34.59% improvement in ADRS over state-of-the-art methods

metrics.other: ADRS improved 34.59% over baseline with 66.67% runtime overhead
